messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Re: problem with pbeta() and random effects
messages.subject_clean: [TMB users] Re: problem with pbeta() and random effects
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Yes, you can file an issue, not so much under the expectation that someone will look into it soon,
but rather to warn other users that there may be a problem with using pbeta in combination with the Laplace approximation.
(I am not aware that this has been tested before). For the record,
if you look into the github-folder \adcomp\TMB\inst\include\tiny_ad\beta you will
see that TMB uses the same code to evaluate pbeta as R does.

As for alternative ways of doing this, I do not see an easy fix. It would be nice
to have "copula library" in TMB. The copula density is a composite function (involving pbeta in your case),
for which one can calculate 1,2,3nd order derivatives by hand, and which can be feeded into TMB via "atomic functions".
(However, this requires understanding of how atomic functions work in TMB). This
may be more computationally effient and more numerically robust. However,
this is not to say that the issue with pbeta is not important.

Hans

messages.body_plain:
It looks like the skew-normal distribution define in TMB is
standardized (i.e. based on a standard N(0,1) distribution).

   I'm guessing that you would want to standardize your response
variable before feeding it to the skew-normal.

   mu = beta0 + beta1*x;
   sd = exp(logsd);
   y0 = (y-mu)/sd;
   nll = -sum(y0, alpha, true);

(This is assuming that you have defined mu as a vector, sd as a scalar,
and logsd as an additional parameter.)

   Just guessing, though.

====

template <class Type>
  Type dsn(Type x, Type alpha, int give_log=0)
  {

          if(!give_log) return 2 * dnorm(x,Type(0),Type(1),0) *
pnorm(alpha*x);
          else return log(2.0) + log(dnorm(x,Type(0),Type(1),0)) +
log(pnorm(alpha*x));
  }

http://kaskr.github.io/adcomp/distributions__R_8hpp_source.html

messages.subject: Older R and Rtools are better for TMB?
messages.subject_clean: Older R and Rtools are better for TMB?
messages.body_plain:
Dear TMB users who use Windows.

I run into differences in compile-link between versions of R and Rtools.  Given the same CPP file, my colleagues’ Window machines (R version: 3.6.3; Rtools version: 3.5) work well whereas my Window machine (R version: 4.0.5; Rtools version: 4.0.0) does not, especially when “std::cout xxx xxx std::endl;” exists.   More importantly the newer versions do not help a user to find error locations when compiling a CPP file, whereas the older versions show error lines and clues about errors.

It would not make sense for TMB users to maintain the *older* versions for getting help with the error locations, because R keeps being updated.  I wonder about how TMB users deal with such problems, and would appreciate your advice or tips.

Saang-Yoon
